extracted.intended_audience: recreational fishery participants, state fish & wildlife agencies, NMFS staff, and other regulated stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive criteria governing inseason transfers of Pacific halibut recreational allocations among Area 2A states (Washington, Oregon, California), and the related public notice/comment and implementation requirements for such temporary rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and regulatory authority
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is issued pursuant to the Northern Pacific Halibut Act of 1982 (16 U.S.C. 773-773k) and the regulatory authority at 50 CFR 300.63(c)(6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All inseason allocation modifications must be grounded in the cited statutory and regulatory authorities; the rule also notes exemption from review under Executive Order 12866.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted basis for inseason transfer (50 CFR 300.63(c)(6)(i)(F))
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations allow NMFS to transfer portions of state recreational allocations inseason to another state under certain circumstances (e.g., if a state is projected to not utilize its respective recreational allocation by the end of the fishing season and another state could utilize additional pounds to avoid closing a fishing season early).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CSP and implementing regulations describe the specific circumstances when transfers are appropriate; transfers should be consistent with the Catch Sharing Plan framework adopted by the IPHC and the Council.

rubrics_metrics.name: Must not result in exceeding the Area 2A catch limit
rubrics_metrics.description: NMFS may modify state recreational allocations provided that the action allows allocation objectives to be met and will not result in exceeding the catch limit for Area 2A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before effectuating a transfer, NMFS evaluates catch projections and available pounds to ensure total Area 2A FCEY (fishery constant exploitation yield) is not exceeded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of best available data and catch projections
rubrics_metrics.description: Transfers are based on the best available information (e.g., catch monitoring reports, state landings data, and fishing rates from previous years) to project whether states will harvest their allocations by season end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NMFS uses updated state landings data (examples: WDFW and ODFW submissions) and historical fishing rates to project attainment; catch monitoring reports from state sampling procedures are used to continue monitoring after a transfer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination with Council staff and state agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: NMFS consults with Council staff and the relevant State Fish and Wildlife agencies (e.g., WDFW, ODFW, California DFW) when determining the need for an inseason transfer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision described consultation with Council staff and three state agencies prior to transferring 12,000 lb from Oregon to Washington; such coordination supports the finding that transfer is necessary and appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited scope of transfers — only unused pounds and only if needed to keep area open
rubrics_metrics.description: Inseason transfers are limited to unused pounds projected to be available from one state and only when another area/state needs those pounds to remain open through its prescribed season dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NMFS may take future inseason action to reallocate additional unused allocation if projections indicate availability and need; transfers are chosen to provide opportunity with little risk of exceeding allocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and necessity — good cause to waive prior notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 5 U.S.C. 553(b)(3)(B), there is good cause to waive prior notice and opportunity for public comment when notice and comment would be impracticable and contrary to the public interest because timely action is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ruleary finding must explain why timely implementation is necessary (e.g., to allow a state fishery to remain open, to allow business and personal decisions by affected parties).

rubrics_metrics.name: Good cause to waive delay of effective date
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 5 U.S.C. 553(d)(3), there can be good cause to waive the 30-day delay in effective date and make the action effective immediately upon filing for public inspection when delay would constrain fishing opportunity or be inconsistent with CSP goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency should articulate how delay would obstruct allocation objectives or economic opportunities; immediate effectiveness may be used for inseason adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment period and process when waivers used
rubrics_metrics.description: Even when prior notice is waived, NMFS will accept public comments for a short post-publication period (here, 15 days) in accordance with 50 CFR 300.63(c)(6)(iv).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document specifies how comments will be accepted and that NMFS may not consider comments submitted by other methods or after the period ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment submission requirements and public record handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments must be identified by docket number (NOAA-NMFS-2024-0014) and submitted via Regulations.gov or by mail to the specified address; all comments become part of the public record and will be posted without change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule warns commenters that personal identifying information or confidential business information submitted voluntarily will be publicly accessible; anonymous comments are accepted (enter 'N/A' in required fields).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and announcement methods for inseason actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Any inseason action, including closures and transfers, will be announced in accordance with 50 CFR 300.63(c) and via the NMFS hotline and state agencies (telephone hotline, news release, and state fish & wildlife agencies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NMFS will publish notices, provide hotline numbers, and coordinate with state agencies to ensure the regulated public is informed promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic and seasonal limits of action
rubrics_metrics.description: This specific inseason transfer applies to IPHC regulatory Area 2A (Washington, Oregon, and California) and is effective for the 2024 seasons (effective September 20, 2024, through December 31, 2024).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfers are tied to state-specific season closure dates (e.g., Washington through September 30; Oregon through October 31; Northern/Southern California dates specified) and may be used only to allow states to meet their season objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale for action — meeting Catch Sharing Plan objectives and economic considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency must justify that the transfer meets management objectives of the CSP, provides anglers additional opportunity to achieve coastwide allocation, and supports economic benefits to fishery participants and associated communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale includes projections showing under- or over-attainment, and emphasizes minimizing risk of exceeding allocations while maximizing attainment and economic opportunity.
